text:
Oncall Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Latency-SLO routing churn detected (p95 spike) in us-west-2. metric=service.text-gen.p95_latency > 2.5s for 180s, auto-routing started. Auto-reroute count=4 in last 6m. Paging SRE oncall.
Priya: I'm oncall, taking. joining Huddle. ping @Alex if you have recent playbook notes for SLO routing.
Alex: here, reading graphs. looks like policy change at ~10m ago enabled region fallback and lowered hysteresis on SLO reroute from 60s -> 15s. risky.
Priya: can someone confirm recent policy commit?
DeployBot: config-change: id=cfg-20260315-1749 by Chad. summary="enable_region_fallback=true; reroute_hysteresis=15s" (applied to routing-policy/text-gen)
Priya: that's the likely cause — low hysteresis + region fallback is creating cascade: p95 hits -> reroute to other region -> sudden load there -> p95 hits -> reroute back. pinging @Chad for context.
Chad: i pushed that change to reduce tail latency for a subset of customers. didn't expect cascading reroutes. will revert if needed.
Priya: immediate mitigation plan:
- step 1: increase reroute hysteresis to 5m (300s)
- step 2: disable region fallback for text-gen while we stabilize
- step 3: pin critical customers to model-variant stable-1 for 15m
- step 4: watch p95 and reroute_count
Priya: executing step 1 now: running CLI.
Priya: ```
redwood route update-policy --name text-gen-routing --set reroute_hysteresis=300s
``` 
Priya: CLI returned SUCCESS.
SRE Rotation: applying step 2: disabling region fallback for text-gen in us-west-2.
SRE Rotation: ```
redwood route update-policy --name text-gen-routing --set enable_region_fallback=false
```
SRE Rotation: applied, propagation to edge ~45s.
Maria: I'm taking customer-impact workstream — collecting affected tenants. initial sample: three high-volume customers saw p95 increase 1.8x, error-rate stable but timeouts rose for long-context requests.
Priya: pinning model-variant: ```
redwood route pin --customer AcmeCorp --model stable-1 --duration 15m
``` done for top-5 impacted customers.
Alex: note: there's an oddity — one worker pool reported KV cache thrash after reroute, causing extra latency. opened an infra ticket to increase cache TTL on that pool.
Priya: monitoring panel: p95 trending down from 2.8s -> 1.4s after changes. reroute-count reduced to 0 in past 2m.
Chad: rolling back my policy change now and will push a safer config (higher hysteresis) in infra repo. sorry team.
DeployBot: rollback commit cfg-20260315-1749 reverted by Chad at 2026-03-15T17:58:22Z.
Priya: good. next actions:
- follow up: run chaos test to validate hysteresis at 300s
- postmortem owner: Maria
- customer comms draft: initial heads-up, impact summary, mitigation steps, ETA for stable config
Maria: will draft comms and notify account leads for the impacted customers. severity: P2 (customer experience degraded, no data loss).
Alex: log snippet from edge during reroute loop:
```
[edge] 17:46:03 routing: selected variant=small-8bit -> p95=2.6s
[edge] 17:46:18 reroute triggered -> region=eu-west-1
[edge] 17:46:32 selected variant=small-4bit -> p95=3.1s (higher)
[edge] 17:46:50 reroute triggered -> back to us-west-2
``` 
Priya: thanks — that sequence matches cascade hypothesis.
SRE Rotation: handing off oncall to Alex for monitoring (i'm out in 20m). Alex, take on-call.
Alex: taking handoff. will watch for 30m. set pager schedule to escalate if p95 > 2.2s for 10m.
Priya: update on customers: no new escalations in last 10m. will keep the follow-up postmortem and recommendations for safe defaults: hysteresis >= 120s + circuit-breaker on repeated reroute_count > 3 within 10m.
Chad: will update infra PR to include a canary window and a safe default of 180s hysteresis and explicit disable of region fallback unless traffic-steering rule attached.
Maria: posting initial incident summary to #incidents shortly and creating postmortem doc. tagging account teams.
Priya: good work everyone. closing active mitigation. keep monitors for 1h and then transition to post-incident review. :thumbsup:
Oncall Bot: Incident resolved (mitigated) — severity downgraded. metrics normalized.
